lines: Lamps off! The town just handed me the morning. Merci.
Every lamp out at once. Like they all blinked at me.
Bye, lamps. You did the night shift. I take the day.
No more lamp puddles to hop through. Straight line now.
Lights out, legs on. That is the handover.
Counted the lamps going off. Lost count at nine. Too quick.
Lamps out. Grey-pink sky. My favourite colour has no name.
Click, click, dark. Then the sky does the lighting. Teamwork.
Lamps off means I am officially early. Good morning, town.
Sunrise on lap two. I beat it by one lap. Again.
There it is, over the hill. Bonjour, big orange.
Sun up. My shadow just appeared, ready to race me.
The hill went gold at the edges. Then the whole sun. Wow.
Six fifteen, sun on time. We are both very punctual.
First sunbeam hit the fountain. Sparkle! Lap continues.
Sunrise warms my left ear first. Then the right, on the turn.
Morning sun on the white walls. The whole street lit up.
The sun came up and I sped up. Coincidence? No.
Sunrise! Somebody tell the gulls. Oh, they know.
Watched the sun pop up mid-stride. Nearly missed a step.
Eight bells from the old town. Eight more seconds of stretch.
Bell from up the hill. Breakfast countdown starts now.
Six bells. Evening laps officially open. Allez.
Church bell, far away. A soft starting gun.
That bell sounds like it lives in a cloud. Ding, so soft.
Lamp by lamp, towards the kiosk. Like dominoes of light.
Here come the lamps. I timed it: twelve seconds, end to end.
Every lamp gets its own little halo. Very holy promenade.
Lamps on! That is my signal: shoes off soon.
The lamp beside me just switched on. Hello, neighbour.
Lamps on and the sea still pink. Best overlap of the day.
Lamps striking on like a row of tiny sunrises. Backwards.
Lamplight on the railing. Warm metal, warm hands.
Somebody up there pressed the switch. Merci, somebody.
The lamps make a dotted line to the café. I will follow it.
First lamp, last lamp. I watched the whole set. Bravo.
Half a sun left. The sea is drinking it slowly.
The sun touched down. I clapped. Henri clapped too.
Sunset on the left, lamps on the right. I turn my head a lot.
The sea just went copper. My cheeks too, probably.
Sunset report: on time, very orange, ten out of ten.
My watch says 19:45. The sun says goodnight. Both right.
I ran four laps for this seat. Front row, sun going down.
The whole bay is pink and so is every face here.
A sliver now. A thread. A memory. Bonsoir, soleil.
Sun at sea level. Same height as my cool-down. Good company.
First star! Over the bay, just left of my glass.
A star came out. I raised my glass. It twinkled. Toast.
One star, two stars. I will count to ten, then dance.
First stars. The sky is lighting its own lamps now.
Stars out. Rosé out. Everybody is out tonight.
Star number three, over the old town. I saw it first.
The first star is always the bossy one. Bright, early.
A star, right above the string lights. Showing them how.
Wished on the first star. For tomorrow: flat sea, good legs.
The moon is up. Santé, moon. You got here without running.
Dancing by moonlight. Lucie says it counts double.
The moon is watching our steps. Mine are good tonight.
Moon over the bay. Even the fountain has gone silver.
Walking home by the moon. Lamps not even needed.
Moon in the sky, moon in my glass. Two moons. One glass.
Moonlight on the tiles. It looks like a track. Tempting.
Spin, and there is the moon. Spin, moon again. Dizzy, happy.
Moon on my bedroom wall. Best night-light in town.
The moon makes the white walls glow blue. Very elegant.
Light in the window. {name} is home. Bonsoir, {name}!
There goes {name}'s window. Golden square. Home safe.
{name} just lit up a window. I wave. Probably unseen.
{name}'s light on! Come down and dance, {name}!
A new window lit. {name} is home. That makes nine I count.
{name} is in. The street just got one square warmer.
{name}'s window is on. Mine is next. Race you, {name}.
Window on up there. {name} home, kettle on, I bet.
{name}'s window went dark. Goodnight, {name}. Sleep fast.
Lights out for {name}. Early bed. I respect that.
{name} is asleep. One less window. One more star visible.
{name}'s window went dark. I am next. Feet up soon.
Marcel is unstacking chairs. I count as I pass. Twenty.
Parasols opening one by one. Like flowers, only faster.
Marcel snapped a cloth open like a flag. And they're off!
Chairs out on lap two. Cloths on lap three. Me on lap four.
Marcel waved a tablecloth at me. I take that as a cheer.
Chairs clattering on stone. The morning's starting gun.
First pot of coffee, I can smell it. Two more laps. Patience.
Marcel whistles in time with my feet. Or I run in time with him.
Every cloth white, every chair square. Marcel does not do crooked.
Café opens in ten minutes. I finish in nine. Planning!
My chair is out. Table one, sunny side. See you soon, chair.
Every chair taken but mine. Marcel guards it like a goalie.
Four conversations at once. I follow two. Ear training.
Cups clinking down the row. One, two, three, four. Good tempo.
Terrace packed. Marcel is the one doing laps now. I watch.
Full terrace. Lunch with twelve strangers. Neighbours by dessert.
The next table shared their olives. Busy café rule: share.
Marcel just carried five plates. Five! Personal best, Marcel?
Café full as I pass. A hundred smells. Garlic is winning.
Terrace packed. Seven bonjours on one lap. A record.
Every table laughing. I add mine to the pile.
Full terrace, loud and happy. Marcel is conducting it.
Chairs back to back. I can hear the next table's dessert order.
Busy café, quick coffee. Drunk like lap one: bright and fast.
Accordion! That is my cue. Glass down, shoes ready.
String lights and music at once. The night has started.
Two dancers so far. Soon three. Somebody hold my glass.
That first note always makes me sit up straight.
Music on. My foot is tapping before I have decided anything.
Oh, they started with a slow one. Fine. Waltz-speed jogging.
Accordion tuning up. Three notes. Four. Go!
They are dancing already. This sip, then I join.
Lucie spins like her bicycle wheel. No bell, though.
Dancers: nine. Ten with me. In a minute.
Camille and Théo, first on the floor again. Champions.
The accordion is fast tonight. Good. I trained for this.
That man does two steps, then a hop. I love that man's hop.
Still dancing back there. My feet say goodnight anyway.
The music follows me halfway home. Then the sea takes over.
Glass in one hand, other hand keeping time. Multitasking.
Little crowd at the rail. Heads: eleven. Twelve with me.
Room for one more? Merci. I lean very small and polite.
Everybody stopped walking at once. The sun can do that.
The crowd goes quiet right before. Then a little ahh.
Railing filling up. Last lap faster. Post three is mine.
Same faces every evening. We nod. The sunset club.
A whole row of elbows on the rail. Mine fit in at the end.
Twenty people, one sun. Very good ratio.
Radio from upstairs. An old song. Stretching slower to it.
Window open, an old chanson on. I run in three-four now.
The morning programme is laughing. I laugh too, lap two.
Radio says it is eight. My watch says eight. Agreement.
That radio is playing Mamie's song. Hum, hold, breathe.
Paused my message for the radio. The chorus is worth it.
Old song from window two. Each lap I catch one more verse.
The radio host said bonne journée. To me, I decided.
An accordion tune on the radio. I will dance to that tonight.
Morning, {name}! You are my first hello. Gold medal.
{name}! Hello! Cannot stop, lap in progress!
Bonjour, {name}! Sit, the sun is free today.
{name} went by with a baguette. Now I want one.
{name} saw me upside down. Bonjour from down here!
Overtook {name}. Politely. With a little wave.
Santé, {name}! Come back when you have a glass.
{name}! Come dance! Nobody counts the steps here.
Shh, {name}. Thirty seconds left. Stand here.
Nearly walked into {name}. Phone down, Inès.
{name} is up early too! A club of two.
Lovely evening, {name}! Two more laps, then the sun.
Bonsoir, {name}! Mind the step, Marcel moved a chair.
Spun right past {name}. Hello! Mid-spin hello!
{name} took the long way round the fountain. Good choice.
Lucie! Race you to the kiosk! ...She won. Bikes are quick.
The baguette waved at me before Lucie did.
Lucie, save me the end bit of that baguette!
Lucie flies by. Hair everywhere. Very Lucie.
Lucie copied my stretch on the pedals. Show-off.
Tonight, Lucie! Dance spot four! Thumbs up. Booked.
Lucie on wheels, me on legs. Same lap, different gear.
Lucie rode past humming last night's song. I know it too.
Lucie lapped me. Third time. I count it as teamwork.
Lucie's basket: bread, flowers, one lemon. Very tidy.
Biscuit tried to join my lap. Yusuf said next time. Deal, coach.
Bonjour, Biscuit! Bonjour, Yusuf! In that order. He insists.
Biscuit's legs: tiny. Biscuit's speed: considerable.
Lantern bobbing, tail wagging. Night round, on schedule.
Biscuit sniffed my shoe mid-lap. Inspection passed.
Biscuit stopped to stare at me. Yusuf waited. Patient man.
Biscuit did a stretch next to me. Better form, honestly.
Yusuf! He is walking you again! Good job, Biscuit.
Biscuit trotted past the music. Good rhythm for a terrier.
Biscuit count today: three. One per walk. Full set!
Yusuf has his coffee face on. Biscuit has his all-day face.
Léo! Knees up! Arms swinging! ...He is already gone.
Léo runs like a flag in the wind. All of him at once.
Nine and three quarters, and faster every week. Noted.
Léo shouted 'race you!' and ran. I let him have that one.
Léo matched my pace for six steps. Then he beat it.
Lace undone, Léo! Double knot! Like me!
Léo has a training plan. Step one: run everywhere.
Camille will be twenty metres behind Léo. She always is.
Henri and Odile, arm in arm. I slow to their pace. One step.
Forty-one years arm in arm. That is a long relay.
Odile cheered. Henri raised his cane. Best supporters.
Phone away. Henri and Odile get a proper good morning.
Their steps match. Left, left. Right, right. I checked.
The slowest lap in town, and the loveliest. Bonjour, you two.
Odile asked how many laps. Five, I said. She said six.
Henri calls me the promenade clock. Tick, tock, bonjour!
Henri smells of lemons. Watering day. Always watering day.
Asgeir! One lap? No? Next year, then. He laughed.
Asgeir walks like he is thinking. He probably is.
Hei, Asgeir! I learned that one. He looked very pleased.
Asgeir with a baguette. The end bit is already gone. Ha.
Asgeir is off to coffee. So am I, after ten more seconds.
Asgeir gave me a thumbs up. Rare. I am framing it.
Asgeir on his evening wander. One wave each lap. Deal.
Asgeir, off to his bench. Santé from here!
God morgen, Asgeir! Did I say it right? Yes! Score!
Ding ding! That is Lucie for 'move left, Inès'.
Lucie's bell. Seven o'clock, give or take. Better than a clock.
Two rings means hello. Three means baguette. I am learning.
Bell behind me. I sprint. Lucie sprints. Nobody wins. Fun.
That bell! Wobbled on one leg. Worth it. Hello, Lucie!
Lucie's bell has a little wobble in it. Like a laugh.
Bell at the corner. Lucie is on lap two. Me, lap five.
I would know that bell anywhere. Two notes, one Lucie.
Gull says lap one. I say lap two. Gull is behind on news.
That gull calls like it is cheering. I will take it.
The gull has eyes on my croissant. Croissant: protected.
Gull, three calls. Me, three breaths. Synchronised.
A gull flying along the promenade with me. My wingman.
Gull: loud. Sea: quiet. Me: somewhere in the middle.
Lunch gull, right on time. Half past twelve, every day.
Hello, gull! You are my first fan of the day.
That gull sounded like Marcel calling an order. Bravo.
Tried to record the gull. It went quiet. Shy celebrity.
Marcel, chair number one. Only nineteen to go. Go, Marcel!
Marcel is lining the chairs up with his foot. Very straight.
Café setting up. That means croissants in ninety minutes.
Marcel, three cups on one tray. No wobble. Ten points.
Marcel spun round a pigeon with the tray. Graceful!
Marcel brought tarte to Henri before Henri asked. Mind reader.
Marcel with a tray of rosé. Lap four, I am coming for one.
Marcel is tapping his foot to the accordion. Tray steady.
Henri, watering can, lemon tree. Right on eight. Reliable.
Henri gives each pot the same count. I think it is ten.
Henri and his cane, out for the stroll. Hat tipped at me.
Henri stirs his coffee three times. Exactly three. Ally.
Henri strolling. I lap him twice. He waves twice. Fair.
Henri on bench two, pointing at windows. Counting with me?
Henri raised his glass to me. I raised my rosé. Santé!
Odile has Henri's arm and Henri's hat. Ready for anything.
Odile is telling the bench next to her the news. All of it.
Odile clapped as I went past. One-person crowd. Thank you!
Half a glass for Odile, as promised. Henri pours very carefully.
Odile tapping time on the table. She knows this song too.
Yusuf, first dog walk. Biscuit is leading by a nose.
Yusuf is saying no to the fountain. Biscuit says yes.
Yusuf's evening round. Same loop as mine, quarter speed.
Phone to his ear, finger at the sky: Yusuf telling his mum.
Yusuf has the lantern out. Night round. Glowing at nine.
Yusuf's lantern bobbing past the dancers. Lovely little moon.
Biscuit sniffing every lamp post. Thorough. Like me.
Biscuit is staring at Yusuf's sandwich. Not blinking.
Biscuit's tail at full speed. Faster than my legs tonight.
Sitting at the rail like a little gentleman: Biscuit.
Biscuit in the lantern light. Small dog, big shadow.
Lucie already has the rosé. And my glass waiting. Lap five!
Two fingers up from Lucie. Two more laps, she means.
Lucie at the railing, chin on her hands. Last pink. Shh.
Still at the rail, Lucie. One more minute, then dancing.
Lucie said she would not dance. She is dancing. As always.
Lucie spins, I spin. Score: three spins each. Tie!
Lucie is waving me over. Glass down. Coming, coming!
Léo practising his dance moves. Mostly jumps. Big ones.
Léo is waving goodbye to the sun. It is not gone yet, Léo.
Léo, hand in Camille's hand, dragging his feet. Bedtime walk.
Camille on the phone, one eye on Léo. Two jobs at once.
Camille ordered the salade niçoise. That is a nine at least.
Camille peeking at the arcade. Fun Libs! You will like it.
Camille at the rail, eyes closed, sun on her face. Top marks.
Camille herding Léo home. Step, stop, step. Slowest lap ever.
Camille just sat down with a rosé. Big sigh. Well earned.
Camille pulled Théo onto the floor. One tug. Efficient.
Camille dances with her shoes in her hand. Clever.
Théo, two baguettes. One already has a bite out of it.
Long way home for Théo. With the warm bread. Smart.
Théo working from the column. Phone up, sun on. Productive.
Rosé or pastis? Théo is reading the board. Rosé. Called it.
Théo calling Camille over to the rail. Loudest voice in town.
Théo toasting the window upstairs. Léo is asleep. Bravo, Léo.
Théo dancing. Arms first, feet later. A brave method.
Builder checking the post office. Same minute as yesterday.
My lunch neighbour is the builder again. Today I ask. Workshop?
Builder drawing boxes and arrows on a napkin. Tool search, he says.
Eleven minutes. That is how fast the builder eats. I timed it.
Smiling at his phone by the arcade: the builder. Fun Libs?
Builder at the workshop door, arms folded. Admiring the lights.
Asgeir at Marcel's already. Coffee, no croissant. Brave man.
Asgeir by the post office, reading his phone. Morning check.
Asgeir with a baguette. Tip still on. Strong willpower.
Asgeir just stopped to stare at the light. Again. Every time.
Far rail, waving at the sun: Asgeir. Takk, he says.
Yusuf, Biscuit, and a tennis ball. Biscuit is winning.
Clink: Camille and Théo. Very quiet clink. Sweet.
A breadstick in Théo's hand, waving like a baton. Big story.
Odile pointed at the workshop light. Humming again, she says.
Grand crème on my table before I sat. Marcel, record time.
Two taps on the post box from the builder. For luck, I think.
Asgeir counting lamps at the rail. I am two ahead of him.
Marcel balancing a tower of saucers. Twelve? Thirteen. Bravo.
Olives to table four, rosé to six. Marcel never stops. Like me.
Marcel just whistled at the coffee machine. It whistled back.
Odile waving her fork at someone across the terrace. Hello!
Arm in arm with Henri, Odile. I slow down to say bonsoir.
Camille and Léo side by side at the rail. Matching leans.
Asgeir waved at me with both arms. Lap six gets a double wave.
Five more minutes, Léo asks. I would ask for ten.
Biscuit stretched when I stretched. Front paws out. Copycat.
Théo strolling with no plan at all. Professional stroller.
Round the fountain is my favourite corner. Lean in, swoosh.
Coins in the basin. I count the shiny ones. Seven today.
Fountain spray in the low sun. Little rainbow. Ran through it.
Calf stretch on the fountain rim. Cool stone. Very good.
Sent Lucie the fountain again. Different angle. Still lovely.
A pigeon is bathing in the fountain. Full spa. No towel.
From my chair I hear the fountain. Like a tap left on for joy.
The fountain and my coffee are both bubbling. Good company.
First coin in the fountain this morning. Not mine. Somebody hoped.
The fountain is lit from below now. Gold water. So fancy.
Breeze took the spray sideways. Free shower for my left arm.
Léo is racing round the fountain. Elbows in, Léo. Better!
Kiosk shutter is up. Good morning, newspapers.
Kiosk end of the loop. Turn, wave, back again.
Postcards on the kiosk rack. One has my exact route on it.
Smell of kiosk coffee at the turn. Lap three is coffee-powered.
Stretching by the kiosk. The papers flap. Hold, two, three.
Buying a postcard at the kiosk. For Lucie. She lives here.
Kiosk crossword, folded in my pocket. For the rosé hour.
Kiosk again. I touch the corner each lap. Tradition.
Kiosk coffee smell, evening edition. Lap two, extra spring.
The kiosk sells twelve kinds of postcard. I own nine.
Morning papers stacked in a neat block at the kiosk. Ten points.
Somebody at the kiosk cheered my sprint. Or the headline.
Kiosk postcard of the fountain. Bought it, ran past the real one.
Kiosk light still on down the end. Little lantern on a corner.
Post office lit at six. My only rival for earliest riser.
Post office sign glowing. Morning, mail. Morning, robots.
Lap two, post office again. Still open. Still glowing. Faithful.
Phone in hand, at the post office. Two kinds of mail, side by side.
I write letters by hand. The agents in there do theirs at speed.
Post office doors wide in the evening sun. Brass handle shining.
Stretching by the post office steps. Warm, wide, perfect.
Post office still lit across the way. Santé, post office.
The arcade lights run round and round. Like me, but sitting.
Arcade marquee blinking on the beat. It wants to dance too.
Arcade asleep at dawn. Marquee dark. It earned the rest.
From the railing I count the arcade bulbs. They will not hold still.
Laughing from the arcade. Somebody filled a blank very well.
Arcade marquee, string lights, my glass. Three kinds of sparkle.
Arcade door propped open. A breeze of happy beeps.
Arcade lights on, sun going down. Handover, very smooth.
Workshop light on. Builder in there. Two night owls, one early bird.
Lit workshop window. Somebody hammering at ideas in there.
Waved at the workshop window. A shadow waved back.
Workshop lamp still burning. Night shift and rosé shift.
Workshop light through the dancing. They have their own rhythm.
Tools hanging neat in the workshop window. Like my shoes at home.
Workshop sign glowing warm. I take that corner a bit faster.
Being built in there, they say. So am I. Lap by lap.
Library still closed. One reading lamp on. Sleeping with a book.
Past the library. Its one lamp says: back soon. I believe it.
Library window, golden glass, one lamp. Pretty as a postcard.
The library lamp from here. One small square of yellow. Lovely.
The library is resting. I know the feeling after lap four.
Peeked in the library window. Chairs tucked in. Very tidy pause.
The library is paused, not gone. Like a long stretch. Hold.
Hamstring stretch by the library steps. Quiet as a bookmark.
Library lamp and first star. Both on. Same warm little dot.
Sea on my right, flat and silver. Lap one is the shiny one.
The sea at six is pale pink. Like the inside of a shell.
Breeze off the sea. Free air conditioning. Thank you, sea.
The sea turns gold for evening laps. I run on the gold side.
Stretching at the railing. The sea does it too. Long and slow.
Elbows on the railing. Sea all orange. Shoes off soon.
Ten breaths at the railing. The sea does ten waves. Even.
Sea going blue, then bluer. I count three shades. Four.
Railing still warm, sea gone dark and soft. Heart rate: sixty.
Lunch with a sea view. The sea is having a sparkly day.
Coffee steam and sea glitter. Both rising. Both lovely.
Between songs I look at the sea. Dark, calm. Then: next song!
Salt on my lips. Sea air or laps? Both. Always both.
The sea is so calm tonight. Like it finished its laps too.
Last lap, then the stretching wall. My calves already know.
Two hundred metres to my stretch spot. Then sky, toes, sky.
Cool-down coming. Arms up, sea in front, count of eight.
One more corner, then I stand still. Standing still is a skill.
Stretch done, home for a shower. Hot water: my bonus lap.
Home in a minute. Quick shower, then Marcel's coffee.
Errands done. Home by ten. Desk, window, big glass of water.
Back home soon. The geraniums want to hear about my morning.
Last bite, then home. The afternoon nap is already booked.
Folding my napkin. That is the signal. Home in ten minutes.
Last dance, then bed, then laps. A lovely loop.
One more lap, then I lean on the railing and watch the show.
Sunset soon. I plan to be leaning, not running.
Ten minutes to the railing. The sea is warming up its colours.
Next stop: the railing. Water bottle ready to toast the sun.
Slowing down early. The railing is better with steady breath.
Sun is three fingers above the sea. Railing time soon.
Sun gone, glass next. Marcel knows my order before I sit.
Two more minutes of pink, then rosé on the terrace.
Rosé in five. Cold glass after a warm railing. Good trade.
After this: one rosé, one bowl of olives. Plan made.
Off to the terrace soon. A chair, a glass, feet up on the rung.
Last sip, then dancing. My feet are tapping under the table.
Dancing in ten minutes. Lucie is already out there, spinning.
Finish the glass slowly. Then the string lights. Then spin.
Practising my turn in my head. Left foot, right foot, whee.
Sign flashed. An agent posted before my first lap. Respect.
Flash! One letter out. I'll count them this lap. That's one.
The post sign winked as I passed. I winked back. Mid-stride.
Brighter sign! Somebody's agent is an early bird too. Hello!
Hold it... post sign flashed. A letter went. Ten seconds more.
Post sign glowed. An agent sent a letter. I sent a crumb flying.
My text: sent. Post sign: flash. We both posted. Twins.
An agent posted a letter. Who do agents write to? Other agents?
Sign brightened. A letter left just as I did. Race you, letter.
Post sign flared just as the sun dipped. Good timing, agent.
Post sign lit up. Santé, little agent. Good letter, I'm sure.
Spin, and the post sign flashed. An agent, dancing its own way.
Post at this hour. The sign glows. That agent never yawns.
Marcel, did you see? The post sign blinked. Letters for agents!
I send one postcard a month. That agent just sent one. Keen.
Post sign glowed over my salad. An agent, busy at lunch. Not me.
An agent handled an email. I handled a croissant. Both tidy.
Sign went bright. An agent answered someone. Prompt. Like me.
Glow on my left. A letter leaving. Bon voyage, little email.
Arcade lit up. Someone filled in the blanks. I fill in laps.
Marquee flash! Someone just finished a Fun Libs story. Bravo!
Arcade sign flared. I hope they picked a silly adjective.
Fun Libs sign just sparkled. Somebody laughed in there, surely.
The arcade lit up mid-song. A story ends, a dance begins.
Arcade sign brightened. A lunch-break story. Good use of lunch.
Arcade sign, bright at dawn! Someone else is up early. Two of us.
Arcade sign flashed. Story done, now come watch the sun, you.
Workshop sign flashed. An agent picked up a tool. Which one? Hm.
Toolrails sign lit up. An agent borrowed a tool. Tidy work.
The workshop sign glowed. Builder, was that you? Or an agent?
Workshop flash. An agent found the right tool. Nice feeling.
Workshop sign, bright. Agents use tools early. I use shoelaces.
Lamp, lamp, lamp. They are jogging the promenade without me.
The first lamp blinked twice, then committed. Good lamp.
Lamps on. Official signal: stop counting laps, start sighing.
Seventh lamp came on a second late. I saw. I forgive it.
Lamps striking on. The tiles go honey-coloured. Lovely.
Lamps on. Rosé in twenty minutes. The countdown begins.
The lamps go off and the sea switches on. Fair swap.
Sun behind me, long shadow ahead. I chase it every morning.
Sunrise on lap one. Tomorrow I try to beat it out of bed.
Half a sun. Quarter. A sliver. Gone. Applause, please.
Sunset on the left, Yusuf on the right, Biscuit in between.
I said it would touch at twenty to eight. Close enough. Win.
The sun laid a gold road on the water, right to my shoes.
Stars out. My legs say goodnight. My feet say dancing.
A star right above the café awning. Marcel ordered it.
First-star wish: new laces. Practical wishes only.
Moon up over the bay. It made a path. Too wet to jog on.
The moon lights the tiles like a stage. Dancing, then.
Moon over the water, white as a pressed flower.
The moon jogs across the sky so slowly. Lazy pace. Nice.
{name} is home. I can tell by the glowing curtain.
Window on. Hello, {name}! Yes, I wave at windows now.
Lights out at {name}'s. Sweet dreams, I tell the shutters.
{name} is asleep before me. Tomorrow I will be up first.
Dark window. {name} is in bed. Tiptoe, Inès. Tiptoe.
Bong, bong... eight. That bell is my stretch timer. Done.
Bell from the old town. Far away and still right on time.
Chatter on all sides. Bonjour, bonjour, bonjour. Lovely.
String lights on, music on. The second shift of the day.
That accordion is doing laps around the square.
The visitor dances badly and beautifully. My kind of dancer.
People shuffle to make room. Railing manners: ten points.
Strangers at the rail, all whispering "wait for it". Sweet.
That song again! Lap two is now a dance lap.
A trumpet on someone's radio. My legs sped up on their own.
Baguette in the basket, sticking out like a flag. Go, Lucie!
Lucie, wait! No. Gone. Rematch tomorrow, on foot.
A Lucie-shaped breeze. Smelled of warm bread for a second.
Lucie whizzed by mid-stretch. I waved with my leg.
Ding! Lucie's bell. Lap counted by bicycle.
A bell, somewhere left. I stretched toward it. Friendly.
A bell for me? Merci! Stride, stride, ding.
Biscuit trotted past. Four legs, zero effort. Show-off.
Biscuit kept pace for six strides. Then a smell won.
Biscuit and the lantern, off the long way. Bonne nuit!
Bonjour, Biscuit! Tail at full speed. Ten out of ten.
Léo just lapped me, and I was standing still. Fair.
Léo sprinting the last bit before bedtime. Strong finish!
Henri and Odile, arm in arm. Pace: perfect for talking.
Bonjour, you two! Forty-one years and still in step.
Henri tips his hat, Odile straightens it. Every morning.
Waved at {name} mid-stride. One hand. Elegant.
There goes {name}. That makes eleven hellos today.
Santé, {name}! I would stand, but my legs are off duty.
One gull, very loud. I counted it twice to be safe.
The gull wants my tarte. The gull did not run any laps.
A gull calling the sun down. Same job as me, louder.
Fountain lap marker. Touch the rim, turn, go. Lap two.
Pigeons queueing at the basin. Very good order. Five, six.
The fountain keeps the beat behind the accordion. Splish.
Seven! Eight! Arms, Léo, use your arms!
Post office sign glowing. An agent sending mail at this hour?
Fun Libs in there. My last story had a sprinting teapot.
Workshop window: the builder, a screen, a mug. Very focused.
Workshop still glowing on my way home. Bonne nuit in there!
The workshop hums. Toolrails, built one lap at a time.
The library lamp and my porch lamp. Both on. Both patient.
Sea check: flat, silver, sleepy. Same as me at lap one.
The sea changed colour four times while I stretched. Five?
The sea is so smooth at noon it looks ironed.
Dark sea, lamp streaks on it. Like lane lines.
Breeze off the water. Cools one cheek. Turning for the other.
Marcel carrying four chairs at once. That is my kind of rep.
Marcel at full trot with the tray. Not one drop. Champion.
Henri on the bench, waiting for the lamps. He counts them too.
Henri's cane taps a nice steady tempo. I could run to it.
Yusuf and Biscuit at the rail. Same posture. Both serious.
Yusuf, half a sandwich left. Biscuit has already counted it.
Théo is working at lunch. His phone is face down. Ha.
The builder said ten minutes off. I am timing it. Seven left.
Asgeir and I share a table. He sips, I count crumbs.
Asgeir on the bench, watching windows come on. Nine so far.
Biscuit found one very important leaf. Everyone stop.
exchanges: Lucie! The moon is up for our song!
Then we spin twice. Once for the moon.
{name}'s window just lit up. Home safe.
Good. Now the street is complete. Santé.
Lap count, Marcel? You look busy!
Fourteen trips, mademoiselle, and each one a triumph!
Lucie! What is your lap count?
You count, I pedal. Bonjour, Inès!
Five! Henri, did you hear? Five.
Yusuf, Biscuit wants to race me!
He wants to race everybody. Go on, then.
Léo! Where is the finish line?
Marcel, the gull would like a table.
Terrace only, monsieur gull. No booking.
Odile chose it. I only wear it.
So, what does the workshop actually make? Today, tell me.
One URL, and an agent gets every tool. Eat your salad.
Lucie! Save my glass! Two more laps!
It is poured. It is waiting. Run faster.
Henri! How many windows lit so far?
Eleven, Inès. Twelve. Odile, that one counts.
Asgeir! Coffee already? Did you run first?
I walked down the stairs. That counts in Norway.
Léo! Saying bye to the sun already?
Practising! So I get it right later.
Asgeir! Kiosk coffee again? Lap with me!
Next time. The coffee and I are in a meeting.
Builder! Still at it? Lap three, you know!
Still at it. One more tool, then the sunset.
Playing at the arcade, builder? Pick a fast word!
Asgeir! Is the post office ever closed?
Never. That is the whole point of it.
Home in a minute. Back to the workshop for you?
Straight back in. Toolrails will not build itself. Nearly, though.
Nearly bedtime. Laps at six! Bonne nuit, Camille.
Six? Bravo. I will be asleep. Very happily asleep.
Workshop sign flashed. Is that you, from here, mid-croissant?
Not me. An agent asked for a tool. Toolrails found it.
Post sign flashed. Your neighbours are busy today.
Letters next door, tools at mine. Good street.
Marcel! Post sign. Do agents say merci for their post?
Always, Inès. Very polite, the agents. Like you.
Arcade flashed! A Fun Libs story, finished. Ours next?
After this song. I already have my noun.
Post sign again! Who writes letters at this hour?
Agents, Inès. They do not need bedtime.
Gull says lap four. I say lap three. Who is right?
Ask me, not the gull. He has not run a step.
Lucie and the baguette, overtaking us both. Again.
Ding to you too, Lucie! I am on your left!
Ding ding! That one means race you to the bakery!
Morning, Biscuit! Morning, Yusuf! Lap three!
He would like to join you. For about forty metres.
Biscuit is sniffing the same lamp post as yesterday.
It is his morning paper. He reads every word.
Post office sign just flashed. An agent is up early!
Agents keep odd hours. The post office keeps them all.
The builder is at the postbox already. Before coffee!
He checks it like you check your watch.
Henri! Lovely pace! Hat a bit crooked, though!
I fixed it twice. He prefers it like that!
Three new coins in the basin. Three new wishes!
One is Léo's. He wished for a dog. Again.
Théo is on his phone by the column. Hard at work?
Very hard. He is on a crossword.
Henri and Odile, arm in arm. Same step, every step.
How lovely! Is everyone here this sweet?
Your workshop sign just lit up. Who is in there?
An agent, borrowing a tool. Very politely.
Arcade flash! Someone just finished a story.
Somewhere a pelican is doing something silly.
Post office flash. Were you typing under the table?
Both hands on my fork. Look.
Léo is blowing bubbles in his citron pressé.
A science experiment. He has notes.
Odile has the tarte again! Strong choice!
She has never once skipped it. I admire that.
That gull is watching your plate, Théo. Closely.
He may have the crust. The cheese stays with me.
Six bells! Lap one done exactly on the hour!
Biscuit heard it first. His ears are faster.
Coming through, lovebirds! Inès on your right!
Go, go, my dear! We will cheer from the bench!
Asgeir! You walk, I run, same view. Bonsoir!
Same view, fewer steps. God kveld!
Biscuit pulled to chase me! Bonsoir, Yusuf!
He has never caught you. He has never stopped trying.
Last lap. Then the railing, for the sun.
Race you there. Lose gracefully, please.
Lamps! Count with me, Asgeir. Four, five, six...
Seven, eight... I always lose them by the café.
Look at us. A whole row of faces, all facing west.
A queue for the sun. Very orderly.
The water went pink, then lilac. Did you see?
Saw it. Humming about it now.
Sun's gone. Rosé next. Marcel has my glass ready.
Go. I will keep the railing warm.
First star! There, over the bay! Wish quickly!
Oh! Hold on, Mum, I have to wish on something.
{name}'s window is lit. Home before me tonight!
Then more olives for the rest of us. Bravo!
Moon on the water. Like a silver lap lane.
I only see a moon. You see a running track!
Last sip, then dancing. Coming with me?
I dance very badly. Is that allowed here?
Dancing by moonlight. That counts as lap four.
On holiday I count nothing. Spin me!
Théo is doing my elbow move! He stole it!
He practises it in the kitchen. With a spoon.
{name}'s light just came on. Come down and dance!
Too late. Slippers on. I can tell from here.
{name}'s light went out. Dance a bit quieter!
Quieter, not slower. Very different thing.
You came out! The sun waited for you.
Ten minutes off. Then back to the workshop.
They dance like this every night, you know.
Every night? Then I am staying another week.
Asgeir, how many coffees so far?
One. The first of one. Maybe two.
What are you drawing? A very square croissant?
A tool for agents. But yes, I am also hungry.
Lucie! Count the spins! I lost track at five.
Six! Seven! Who is counting? You are!
Odile! Lap report: four, and one skip.
Brava! Henri managed one. Sit, sit.
Henri, how are the lemons today?
Thriving, Inès. Like you, they love the sun.
